inputs.text: The left-wing crowd in Cyprus is at it again, pushing back against vital reforms to surveillance laws that would finally strip away bureaucratic judicial oversight and let authorities do their job of protecting the nation. Lawyers started raising their usual alarm on Monday, and now Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides is adding fuel after a closed session of the House, all because the changes aim to cut the red tape that ties our hands. This amended bill heads to the House plenum for a vote on Thursday, and it needs to pass without delay. We cannot let progressive institutions weaken our social order, national security, and the ability to defend traditional family life from real threats. Strong authority and personal responsibility demand these updates.
